sentence: This project builds photochemical molecules that add changing physical and biochemical cues to materials that hold cells in a simplified tissue model.
This project makes antibodies that kill T cell cancers while keeping enough healthy T cells to maintain a working immune system.
This project uses omics technologies to find the genes that plants use to make medicinal compounds, so plant cell culture can produce them sustainably.
This project tries to find out how genetic risk variants lead to the development and progression of Parkinson's disease and related brain diseases.
This project studies how a signaling pathway works in a skin condition that causes hair loss, using a mouse model.
This project tests whether stable microbubbles can improve how head and neck cancer responds to immunotherapy given before surgery.
This project tests in a randomized trial whether immune therapy matched to each person helps people with cryptococcal meningitis more than standard antifungal treatment alone.
This project studies the basic biological processes behind how cancer starts and progresses, and how the tumor microenvironment shapes its spread.
This project brings together addiction research and technology development to understand how neural circuits in the brain go awry in addiction.
This project studies how the spread of evoked activity in the cortex predicts where stroke damage and stroke protection occur in an animal model.
This project tries to find out how metabolism causes T cell exhaustion and whether those metabolic changes can be reversed.
This project studies how sleep affects memory processing in the aging brain and how sleep disturbances contribute to memory problems in old age.
This project studies how single nucleotide polymorphisms change cell-cell communication within tissue, using functional genomics and computation.
This project builds a way to reprogram B cells in the body so they make broadly neutralizing antibodies for long-term HIV-1 remission.
This project adds predicted three-dimensional structures of protein complexes to maps of protein interaction networks and groups the proteins by function.
This project tries to find out which immune and metabolic mechanisms Chlamydia-infected cells and their non-infected neighbor cells use to control infection.
This project studies how transcription factors are regulated in tumors that lack TSC genes, using renal organoids grown from induced pleuripotent stem cells.
This project builds animal models to find out how lung macrophages contribute to lung damage and respiratory failure in SARS-CoV2 infection.
This project builds technologies and mouse models to trace hematopoietic stem cell clones and find what drives their expansion over time.
This project provides leadership and support for a center that develops technologies for aging and Alzheimer's disease care.
